summary:
Third review of phase B (sub-mv1jn1fv-01d4cc9d, 116 artifacts), responding to rev-mv1ijr52-01b2f4b6. Every check below was re-run on the final tree after the submission.

Baseline:
- npm test passes 390/390 (ev:ev-mv1jozth-01485646).
- Each task's declared command passes: b1 188 (ev:ev-mv1jutcs-01febe09), b2 119 (ev:ev-mv1jv3k8-01ae4b0c), b4 9 (ev:ev-mv1jv3wd-01166e01), b3 390 plus clean checkout (ev:ev-mv1jvwq5-01042767).
- The artifact list equals the ownership set: 114 owned files, 0 missing (ev:ev-mv1jvx1j-0153189b).

SEC-B-1, the new exact subset search:
- It agrees with my independent brute force on 3000 random catalogs under the old seed and under a fresh one, on best plan, rejections, candidate codes and relaxations (ev:ev-mv1ju6ix-019711e2, ev:ev-mv1ju719-01803407).
- It agrees with the frozen reference planner on 1497 fresh-seed medium catalogs, comparing the full output (ev:ev-mv1jtj32-0105247e).
- The security sweep now passes: the 10,000-cup, stock-100 case answers A in 0.1 ms, and the worst call is 38 ms (ev:ev-mv1ju5yu-01993413).

The stated residual: deliberately tie-laden inputs. I probed it myself (ev:ev-mv1ju48g-01caf1f8):
- On the catalog version one can actually produce (the five seeded products, which suppliers can only re-price, re-time and restock), 1500 adversarial tie-laden calls never reach PLANNER_LIMIT; worst 96 ms, p99 11 ms. A supplier-reachable grid of 400 calls is also clean (worst 1.9 ms).
- The cap is reached only on catalogs no version-one route can create: 0.13 % with C confirmed compatible, and 9.4 % with 12 tie-priced offers. Even there it is bounded at 127-291 ms per call.
I therefore resolve SEC-B-1's major and keep the residual as a minor (SEC-B-1R) with RISK-19, FU-1 and FU-8.

Also resolved:
- SEC-B-2: REPLACE is refused with recursive_triggers=1 (ev:ev-mv1jrept-0107908e).
- SEC-B-3: bodies deeper than 32 levels get 422, and the HTTP canonicalJson refuses depth above 32 with TypeError. My independent probe and the hardening tests pass (ev:ev-mv1jyx54-01238917, ev:ev-mv1jyy8n-01a6c4f3). The security reviewer's HTTP probe (ev-mv1jrhzy-0128826d) exits 1 only on its obsolete RangeError expectation, so it is not cited as support.
- SEC-B-4: slow connections are closed with 408 at 10-11 s and 30 s (ev:ev-mv1jt95x-01f7eff9).

findings.title: Residual: tie-laden catalogs beyond version one's reachable catalog still reach PLANNER_LIMIT, bounded at about 0.1-0.3 s per call
findings.detail:
My probe (ev:ev-mv1ju48g-01caf1f8) measured three catalog kinds:
- Seeded products, which is all that PATCH can produce: 1500 adversarial calls, 0 refusals, worst 96 ms.
- C confirmed compatible: 0.13 % refusals, worst refused call 127 ms.
- 12 tie-priced offers: 9.4 % refusals, worst 291 ms.
No version-one route can produce the last two. Products and offers come from the seed, and a PATCH only versions the existing offer of an existing product. No route writes compatibility rows. Random-priced 12-offer catalogs pass (the engineer's 150-catalog test, and the NFR5 generator).
My previous resolution condition asked for exact and fast results up to 12 offers. That holds for random prices but not for adversarial ties at 12 offers. I downgrade the remainder from major to minor for three reasons: it is unreachable through version one's API (verified); the cap bounds each call (at most about 0.3 s measured); and c2's typed 422 (FU-1) and per-customer planning rate limit (FU-8) plus RISK-19 cover it if the catalog ever grows.
findings.recommendation: Owners: c2-requests-plans-view (FU-1: PLANNER_LIMIT mapped to a typed 422; FU-8: per-customer planning rate limit, which f1 applies to re-plan drains), and the orchestrator (RISK-19). Any future route that creates offers or compatibility rows must first bring the planner to exact and fast on that larger envelope (for example an integer DP over coverage) or cap the catalog. Resolved when FU-1 and FU-8 are proven in phase C and RISK-19 is either closed or carries this condition.

findings.title: Two canonicalJson implementations; only the HTTP one has a depth limit
findings.detail: src/http/body.js exports a depth-limited canonicalJson (TypeError above 32 levels). src/domain/canonical.js exports a different recursive canonicalJson (used for planHash, offersHash and fingerprints per its header). It has cycle and type checks but no depth limit, and it encodes -0 as 0 while the HTTP one uses JSON.stringify. Neither has a caller in src/ yet. Request bodies cannot exceed 32 levels because readJsonBody refuses them first; my probe confirms the domain encoder handles that deepest accepted body (ev:ev-mv1jyx54-01238917).
findings.recommendation: c-phase route tasks (idempotency fingerprints, planHash) should use one canonical encoder, so the same body cannot produce two different fingerprints, and should only feed it values that passed readJsonBody's depth limit. No change needed in phase B.

resolvedFindings.resolution: The per-offer DFS is replaced by an exact subset search (search.js). It agrees with my brute force on 2 x 3000 random catalogs and with the frozen reference on 1497 medium catalogs, on full output. The security sweep passes: the stock-100, 10,000-cup case gives A in 0.1 ms, worst 38 ms. A named timing test was added (planner-sec-b1.test.js). On every catalog version one can produce, adversarial ties never reach the cap. The residual beyond version one's reachable envelope is tracked as SEC-B-1R (minor), RISK-19, FU-1 and FU-8.

openDb sets PRAGMA recursive_triggers = ON. The security reviewer's probe on the final tree shows INSERT OR REPLACE and REPLACE INTO refused for audit_events and inventory_ledger, with plain appends still allowed. SEC-B-2 tests were added to triggers.test.js.

readJsonBody refuses JSON nested deeper than 32 levels with 422 VALIDATION_FAILED, using a non-recursive text scan before JSON.parse. The HTTP canonicalJson stays recursive but refuses depth above 32 with TypeError, so it cannot overflow the stack.
My independent probe passes:
- 20,000-deep and 33-deep text is refused, and 32 levels are accepted.
- Brackets inside strings are ignored.
- canonicalJson throws TypeError on 20,000-deep objects and arrays.
The hardening tests pass 7/7. The security reviewer's HTTP probe (ev-mv1jrhzy-0128826d) exits 1 only on its obsolete expectation that canonicalJson throws RangeError; that is consistent with the fix, but I do not cite it because it failed.
Recorded as FU-10 for c6: the rs14-db-busy test starts the server before the lock holder takes BEGIN IMMEDIATE.

The server uses connectionsCheckingInterval 1000 and maxConnections 512, and answers timeouts with 408. In the slowloris probe, slow-header connections close at 10-11 s and slow bodies at 30 s, all with 408. The SEC-B-4 hardening tests pass.

Resolved or routed:
- SEC-B-5: an existing data/ is tightened to 0700, with a test.
- SEC-B-9: FU-11 for c1.
- SEC-B-6 (lockfile): decision FU-12.
- The README notes go to FU-9 for g2.
- SEC-B-7 and SEC-B-8 stay info as accepted.
